item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Anvi studies the diagram of two rectangles. Both have perimeter $24\,\mathrm{cm}$. Rectangle $P$ is $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $4\,\mathrm{cm}$; rectangle $Q$ is $9\,\mathrm{cm}$ by $3\,\mathrm{cm}$.

Which claim correctly decides what the equal perimeters tell about area?

options.A: The areas must be equal because both shapes are labelled with the word perimeter.
options.C: The perimeters match but the areas differ ($32\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ versus $27\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$), so perimeter alone does not fix area.
options.D: Each area is $24\,\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ because $24$ is the number printed as the perimeter.
